notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.psouffle: The Soufflé program is compiled into a C++ program, which then runs: the time is both, the compilation's added to the run's, though PSouffle's paper times the run alone. PSouffle prints probabilities with eight decimals.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.psouffle: The Soufflé program is compiled into a C++ program, which then runs: the time is both, the compilation's added to the run's, though PSouffle's paper times the run alone. PSouffle prints probabilities with eight decimals.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.psouffle: The Soufflé program is compiled into a C++ program, which then runs: the time is both, the compilation's added to the run's, though PSouffle's paper times the run alone. PSouffle prints probabilities with eight decimals.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.psouffle: The Soufflé program is compiled into a C++ program, which then runs: the time is both, the compilation's added to the run's, though PSouffle's paper times the run alone. PSouffle prints probabilities with eight decimals.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.psouffle: The Soufflé program is compiled into a C++ program, which then runs: the time is both, the compilation's added to the run's, though PSouffle's paper times the run alone. PSouffle prints probabilities with eight decimals.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

#lang roulette/example/disrupt
;; nsym4.dice.dice, translated by tddlog's scripts/dice2roulette.py.

(define complement?
  (not (member "--no-complement" (vector->list (current-command-line-arguments)))))

;; Integers: lists of Booleans, least significant bit first.
(define (bxor a b) (! (<=> a b)))
(define (bv-add xs ys [c #f])
  (if (null? xs)
      '()
      (let* ([x (car xs)] [y (car ys)] [s (bxor x y)])
        (cons (bxor s c) (bv-add (cdr xs) (cdr ys) (|| (&& x y) (&& c s)))))))
(define (bv-sub xs ys) (bv-add xs (map ! ys) #t))
(define (bv-mul xs ys)
  (define w (length xs))
  (for/fold ([acc (make-list w #f)]) ([y (in-list ys)] [i (in-naturals)])
    (if (eq? y #f)
        acc
        (bv-add acc (append (make-list i #f) (for/list ([x (in-list (take xs (- w i)))]) (&& y x)))))))
(define (bv-eq xs ys) (apply && (map <=> xs ys)))
(define (bv-ult xs ys)
  (for/fold ([lt #f]) ([x (in-list xs)] [y (in-list ys)])
    (|| (&& (! x) y) (&& (<=> x y) lt))))
(define (bv-shl xs k)
  (define w (length xs))
  (take (append (make-list (min k w) #f) xs) w))
(define (bv-shr xs k)
  (define j (min k (length xs)))
  (append (drop xs j) (make-list j #f)))

;; Dice's categorical (gen_discrete): from the most significant bit down,
;; bit k is a flip whose probability is the mass of the values with bit k
;; set among those that agree on the bits above, over their mass; one flip
;; for each distinct ratio, chosen by the bits above, settings of no mass
;; left out.
(define (discrete w ps)
  (define size (expt 2 w))
  (define given (list->vector ps))
  (define masses
    (for/vector ([i (in-range size)])
      (if (< i (vector-length given)) (inexact->exact (vector-ref given i)) 0)))
  (define (mass lo hi) (for/sum ([i (in-range lo hi)]) (vector-ref masses i)))
  (let level ([k (sub1 w)] [above '()])
    (cond
      [(< k 0) (reverse above)]
      [else
       (define span (expt 2 (add1 k)))
       (define flips (make-hash))
       (define table
         (for/vector ([u (in-range (quotient size span))])
           (define lo (* u span))
           (define total (mass lo (+ lo span)))
           (cond
             [(zero? total) 'none]
             [else
              (define r (exact->inexact (/ (mass (+ lo (quotient span 2)) (+ lo span)) total)))

# nsym4.pl: a ProbLog program written in Julia for Alea.jl by tddlog's
# scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a
# dictionary from its tuples to whether each holds, a Dist{Bool} of the coins
# or a Bool; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from
# the facts file FACTS; each rule is a loop over the relations its body
# joins. `model()` is the queries' holdings, given the evidence (`observe`),
# in the form of tddlog's data/alea programs: Alea.jl answers them with `pr`,
# and its tddlog backend writes their circuit for tddlog.
#
#   julia --project=ALEA alea_bench.jl run --file FACTS FACTS_PATH problog.jl
using Alea

const QUERY = :pr
const FACTS = ""   # the facts file (alea_bench.jl --file FACTS PATH)

const Relation = Dict{Tuple,Any}
const NONE = Pair{Tuple,Any}[]

# the tuple t of r holds also where x does
add!(r::Relation, t::Tuple, x) = (r[t] = haskey(r, t) ? r[t] | x : x; nothing)
# whether the tuple t of r holds
holds(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = get(r, t, false)
# whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
probe(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = haskey(r, t) ? (r[t],) : ()
# the tuples of r and whether each holds, by their values at positions ps
function index(r::Relation, ps...)
    ix = Dict{Tuple,Vector{Pair{Tuple,Any}}}()
    for (t, x) in r
        push!(get!(() -> Pair{Tuple,Any}[], ix, map(p -> t[p], ps)), t => x)
    end
    ix
end
# whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
holds_any(ix, k) = reduce(|, (x for (_, x) in get(ix, k, NONE)); init = false)
# the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
# head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
function choose(ps...)
    chosen, none, left = Any[], true, 1.0
    for p in ps
        q = left > 0 ? min(p / left, 1.0) : 1.0
        c = q >= 1.0 ? true : flip(q)
        push!(chosen, none & c)
        none, left = none & !c, left - p
    end
    chosen
end

constant(s) = something(tryparse(Int, s), tryparse(Float64, s), Some(Symbol(s)))
# the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
# a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
function facts(path)
    db = Dict{String,Relation}()
    for line in eachline(path)
        f = split(line, '\t')
        p = parse(Float64, f[2])
        add!(get!(Relation, db, f[1]), Tuple(constant.(f[3:end])), p >= 1 ? true : flip(p))
    end
    db
end

function program(db)
    person_facts = get(db, "person/1", Relation())
    friend_facts = get(db, "friend/2", Relation())

    friend = friend_facts

    influences = Relation()
    # 0.2::influences(X,Y) :- friend(X,Y).
    for ((X, Y), x1) in friend
        add!(influences, (X, Y), x1 & flip(0.2))
    end

    person = person_facts

    stress = Relation()
    # 0.3::stress(X) :- person(X).
    for ((X,), x1) in person
        add!(stress, (X,), x1 & flip(0.3))
    end

    # smokes/1: recursive; the rules applied in stages from no tuple, each
    # reading the stage before, until a stage adds no tuple and the stages number the tuples
    smokes = Relation()
    stage, before = 0, -1
    while stage < length(smokes) || length(smokes) != before
        before = length(smokes)
        next_smokes = Relation()
        # smokes(X) :- stress(X).
        for ((X,), x1) in stress
            add!(next_smokes, (X,), x1)
        end
        # smokes(X) :- friend(X,Y), influences(Y,X), smokes(Y).
        for ((X, Y), x1) in friend
            for x2 in probe(influences, (Y, X))
                for x3 in probe(smokes, (Y,))
                    add!(next_smokes, (X,), x1 & x2 & x3)
                end
            end
        end
        smokes = next_smokes
        stage += 1
    end

    queries = (holds(smokes, (:p1,)), holds(smokes, (:p2,)), holds(smokes, (:p3,)), holds(smokes, (:p4,)))
    evidence = true
    queries, evidence
end

# The queries' holdings, the evidence observed: Alea's `@alea` keeps the
# observation, and the relations are built outside it, as plain Julia.
function model()
    qs, ev = program(facts(FACTS))
    ev === true && return qs
    @alea begin
        observe(ev)
        qs
    end
end

;; nsym16.pl: a ProbLog program written in Pluck by tddlog's scripts/problog2ppl.py,
;; first order as it is written. A relation is a list of its tuples, each (Pair
;; TUPLE HOLDING), a symbol a constructor of its own and an integer a natural;
;; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), drawn once; each rule a
;; concat_map over the relations its body joins, a tuple that several instances
;; give holding where one does (`union`). Query cK asks the K-th query, given the
;; evidence.

(define-type weight (Sure) (Chance p))
(define (draw w) (match w Sure => (True) Chance p => (flip p)))
(define (draw_all fs) (map (lambda f -> (Pair (fst f) (draw (snd f)))) fs))
;; rel with the tuple t, holding where v does too
(define (insert eq t v rel)
  (match rel
    Nil => (Cons (Pair t v) (Nil))
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) t) (Cons (Pair t (or (snd e) v)) rest) (Cons e (insert eq t v rest)))))
(define (union eq rel xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => rel
    Cons x rest => (union eq (insert eq (fst x) (snd x) rel) rest)))
;; whether the tuple t of rel holds; whether one of the tuples that p accepts does
(define (holds eq rel t)
  (match rel
    Nil => (False)
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) t) (snd e) (holds eq rest t))))
(define (any_holds p rel)
  (match rel
    Nil => (False)
    Cons e rest => (if (p (fst e)) (or (snd e) (any_holds p rest)) (any_holds p rest))))
(define (concat_map f xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => (Nil)
    Cons x rest => (append (f x) (concat_map f rest))))
(define (between lo hi) (if (> lo hi) (Nil) (Cons lo (between (S lo) hi))))
(define (size_of rels) (fold (lambda acc r -> (+ acc (length r))) 0 rels))
;; the coins of a probabilistic rule in a recursion, kept by instance across the stages: the
;; instances xs, each (Pair KEY (Pair BODY HEADS)), with the coin of each KEY in table (a new
;; one drawn where it has none): (Pair TABLE' the heads, each (Pair TUPLE HOLDING))
(define (coin_of eq k table)
  (match table
    Nil => (Pair (False) (False))

          (more (attach eq draw pick table2 rest))

#lang roulette/example/disrupt
;; nsym12.pl: a ProbLog program written for Roulette by tddlog's
;; scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a hash
;; from its tuples (lists of constants) to whether each holds, a Boolean of the
;; coins; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from the
;; facts file named on the command line; each rule is a loop over the
;; relations its body joins. Each query's distribution is Roulette's, at the
;; module's level (`display-pmf`), given the evidence; the program prints
;; `roulette K true P` and `roulette K false P` for the K-th query.

(require racket/port racket/string racket/match)

;; A statement of the program: a definition, which the language does not
;; run as a query of its own (it runs each expression of the module as one).
(define-syntax-rule (statement e ...) (define-values () (begin e ... (values))))

;; the tuple t of r holds also where x does
(define (add! r t x)
  (hash-set! r t (if (hash-has-key? r t) (|| (hash-ref r t) x) x)))
;; whether the tuple t of r holds
(define (holds r t) (hash-ref r t #f))
;; whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
(define (probe r t) (if (hash-has-key? r t) (list (hash-ref r t)) null))
;; the tuples of r and whether each holds, (tuple . holding) each, by their
;; values at positions ps (from 0)
(define (index r . ps)
  (define ix (make-hash))
  (for ([(t x) (in-hash r)])
    (hash-update! ix (for/list ([p (in-list ps)]) (list-ref t p)) (λ (es) (cons (cons t x) es)) null))
  ix)
;; whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
(define (holds-any ix k)
  (for/fold ([some #f]) ([e (in-list (hash-ref ix k null))]) (|| some (cdr e))))
;; the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
;; head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
(define (choose . ps)
  (let loop ([ps ps] [left 1.0] [none #t])
    (if (null? ps)
        null
        (let* ([q (if (> left 0) (min 1.0 (/ (car ps) left)) 1.0)]
               [c (if (>= q 1.0) #t (flip q))])
          (cons (&& none c) (loop (cdr ps) (- left (car ps)) (&& none (! c))))))))

(define (constant s) (or (string->number s) (string->symbol s)))
;; the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
;; a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
(define (facts path)
  (define db (make-hash))
  (for ([line (in-lines (open-input-file path))])

# nsym10.pl: a ProbLog program written in Julia for Alea.jl by tddlog's
# scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a
# dictionary from its tuples to whether each holds, a Dist{Bool} of the coins
# or a Bool; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from
# the facts file FACTS; each rule is a loop over the relations its body
# joins. `model()` is the queries' holdings, given the evidence (`observe`),
# in the form of tddlog's data/alea programs: Alea.jl answers them with `pr`,
# and its tddlog backend writes their circuit for tddlog.
#
#   julia --project=ALEA alea_bench.jl run --file FACTS FACTS_PATH problog.jl
using Alea

const QUERY = :pr
const FACTS = ""   # the facts file (alea_bench.jl --file FACTS PATH)

const Relation = Dict{Tuple,Any}
const NONE = Pair{Tuple,Any}[]

# the tuple t of r holds also where x does
add!(r::Relation, t::Tuple, x) = (r[t] = haskey(r, t) ? r[t] | x : x; nothing)
# whether the tuple t of r holds
holds(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = get(r, t, false)
# whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
probe(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = haskey(r, t) ? (r[t],) : ()
# the tuples of r and whether each holds, by their values at positions ps
function index(r::Relation, ps...)
    ix = Dict{Tuple,Vector{Pair{Tuple,Any}}}()
    for (t, x) in r
        push!(get!(() -> Pair{Tuple,Any}[], ix, map(p -> t[p], ps)), t => x)
    end
    ix
end
# whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
holds_any(ix, k) = reduce(|, (x for (_, x) in get(ix, k, NONE)); init = false)
# the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
# head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
function choose(ps...)
    chosen, none, left = Any[], true, 1.0
    for p in ps
        q = left > 0 ? min(p / left, 1.0) : 1.0
        c = q >= 1.0 ? true : flip(q)
        push!(chosen, none & c)
        none, left = none & !c, left - p
    end
    chosen
end

constant(s) = something(tryparse(Int, s), tryparse(Float64, s), Some(Symbol(s)))
# the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
# a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
function facts(path)
    db = Dict{String,Relation}()
    for line in eachline(path)
        f = split(line, '\t')
        p = parse(Float64, f[2])
        add!(get!(Relation, db, f[1]), Tuple(constant.(f[3:end])), p >= 1 ? true : flip(p))
    end
    db
end

function program(db)
    person_facts = get(db, "person/1", Relation())
    friend_facts = get(db, "friend/2", Relation())

    friend = friend_facts

    influences = Relation()
    # 0.2::influences(X,Y) :- friend(X,Y).
    for ((X, Y), x1) in friend
        add!(influences, (X, Y), x1 & flip(0.2))
    end

    person = person_facts

    stress = Relation()
    # 0.3::stress(X) :- person(X).
    for ((X,), x1) in person
        add!(stress, (X,), x1 & flip(0.3))
    end

    # smokes/1: recursive; the rules applied in stages from no tuple, each
    # reading the stage before, until a stage adds no tuple and the stages number the tuples
    smokes = Relation()
    stage, before = 0, -1
    while stage < length(smokes) || length(smokes) != before
        before = length(smokes)
        next_smokes = Relation()
        # smokes(X) :- stress(X).
        for ((X,), x1) in stress
            add!(next_smokes, (X,), x1)
        end
        # smokes(X) :- friend(X,Y), influences(Y,X), smokes(Y).
        for ((X, Y), x1) in friend
            for x2 in probe(influences, (Y, X))
                for x3 in probe(smokes, (Y,))
                    add!(next_smokes, (X,), x1 & x2 & x3)
                end
            end
        end
        smokes = next_smokes
        stage += 1
    end

    queries = (holds(smokes, (:p1,)), holds(smokes, (:p2,)), holds(smokes, (:p3,)), holds(smokes, (:p4,)), holds(smokes, (:p5,)), holds(smokes, (:p6,)), holds(smokes, (:p7,)), holds(smokes, (:p8,)), holds(smokes, (:p9,)), holds(smokes, (:p10,)))
    evidence = true
    queries, evidence
end

# The queries' holdings, the evidence observed: Alea's `@alea` keeps the
# observation, and the relations are built outside it, as plain Julia.
function model()
    qs, ev = program(facts(FACTS))
    ev === true && return qs
    @alea begin
        observe(ev)
        qs
    end
end

;; nsym10.pl: a ProbLog program written in Pluck by tddlog's scripts/problog2ppl.py,
;; first order as it is written. A relation is a list of its tuples, each (Pair
;; TUPLE HOLDING), a symbol a constructor of its own and an integer a natural;
;; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), drawn once; each rule a
;; concat_map over the relations its body joins, a tuple that several instances
;; give holding where one does (`union`). Query cK asks the K-th query, given the
;; evidence.

(define-type weight (Sure) (Chance p))
(define (draw w) (match w Sure => (True) Chance p => (flip p)))
(define (draw_all fs) (map (lambda f -> (Pair (fst f) (draw (snd f)))) fs))
;; rel with the tuple t, holding where v does too
(define (insert eq t v rel)
  (match rel
    Nil => (Cons (Pair t v) (Nil))
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) t) (Cons (Pair t (or (snd e) v)) rest) (Cons e (insert eq t v rest)))))
(define (union eq rel xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => rel
    Cons x rest => (union eq (insert eq (fst x) (snd x) rel) rest)))
;; whether the tuple t of rel holds; whether one of the tuples that p accepts does
(define (holds eq rel t)
  (match rel
    Nil => (False)
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) t) (snd e) (holds eq rest t))))
(define (any_holds p rel)
  (match rel
    Nil => (False)
    Cons e rest => (if (p (fst e)) (or (snd e) (any_holds p rest)) (any_holds p rest))))
(define (concat_map f xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => (Nil)
    Cons x rest => (append (f x) (concat_map f rest))))
(define (between lo hi) (if (> lo hi) (Nil) (Cons lo (between (S lo) hi))))
(define (size_of rels) (fold (lambda acc r -> (+ acc (length r))) 0 rels))
;; the coins of a probabilistic rule in a recursion, kept by instance across the stages: the
;; instances xs, each (Pair KEY (Pair BODY HEADS)), with the coin of each KEY in table (a new
;; one drawn where it has none): (Pair TABLE' the heads, each (Pair TUPLE HOLDING))
(define (coin_of eq k table)
  (match table
    Nil => (Pair (False) (False))
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) k) (Pair (True) (snd e)) (coin_of eq k rest))))
(define (attach eq draw pick table xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => (Pair table (Nil))
    Cons x rest =>
    (let ((found (coin_of eq (fst x) table))
          (c (if (fst found) (snd found) (draw)))
          (table2 (if (fst found) table (Cons (Pair (fst x) c) table)))
          (more (attach eq draw pick table2 rest))
          (body (fst (snd x))))
      (Pair (fst more) (append (mapi (lambda h i -> (Pair h (and body (pick c i)))) (snd (snd x))) (snd more))))))

    Nil => (Pair table (Nil))
    Cons x rest =>
    (let ((found (coin_of eq (fst x) table))
          (c (if (fst found) (snd found) (draw)))
          (table2 (if (fst found) table (Cons (Pair (fst x) c) table)))
          (more (attach eq draw pick table2 rest))
          (body (fst (snd x))))

  (Cons (Pair (T1 (c_p2)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T1 (c_p3)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T1 (c_p4)) (Sure))
  (Nil))))))
;; friend/2: 12 facts
(define friend_facts

  (Cons (Pair (T2 (c_p1) (c_p2)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T2 (c_p3) (c_p2)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T2 (c_p2) (c_p3)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T2 (c_p3) (c_p1)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T2 (c_p1) (c_p3)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T2 (c_p4) (c_p3)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T2 (c_p3) (c_p4)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T2 (c_p4) (c_p2)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T2 (c_p2) (c_p4)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T2 (c_p4) (c_p1)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T2 (c_p1) (c_p4)) (Sure))
  (Nil))))))))))))))

  (let ((person_base (draw_all person_facts))
        (friend_base (draw_all friend_facts))
        (friend friend_base)
        (rule2 (concat_map (lambda e1 -> (match (fst e1) T2 vX vY => (Cons (Cons (Pair (T2 vX vY) (and (snd e1) (flip 0.2))) (Nil)) (Nil)))) friend))
        (influences (union eq_influences (Nil) (map (lambda x -> (index 0 x)) rule2)))
        (person person_base)

        (stress (union eq_stress (Nil) (map (lambda x -> (index 0 x)) rule1)))
        (stage3 (lambda rels -> (let ((smokes (index 0 (fst rels)))
        (rule3 (concat_map (lambda e5 -> (match (fst e5) T1 vX => (Cons (Cons (Pair (T1 vX) (snd e5)) (Nil)) (Nil)))) stress))
        (rule4 (concat_map (lambda e6 -> (match (fst e6) T2 vX vY => (concat_map (lambda e9 -> (match (fst e9) T2 a7 a8 => (if (and (constructor=? a7 vY) (constructor=? a8 vX)) (concat_map (lambda e11 -> (match (fst e11) T1 a10 => (if (constructor=? a10 vY) (Cons (Cons (Pair (T1 vX) (and (snd e6) (and (snd e9) (snd e11)))) (Nil)) (Nil)) (Nil)))) smokes) (Nil)))) influences))) friend)))
      (Pair (Cons (union eq_smokes (Nil) (append (map (lambda x -> (index 0 x)) rule3) (map (lambda x -> (index 0 x)) rule4))) (Nil)) (Nil)))))

        (q13 (holds eq_smokes smokes (T1 (c_p2))))
        (q14 (holds eq_smokes smokes (T1 (c_p3))))
        (q15 (holds eq_smokes smokes (T1 (c_p4)))))
    (Pair (True) (Cons q12 (Cons q13 (Cons q14 (Cons q15 (Nil))))))))

#lang roulette/example/disrupt
;; nsym10.pl: a ProbLog program written for Roulette by tddlog's
;; scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a hash
;; from its tuples (lists of constants) to whether each holds, a Boolean of the
;; coins; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from the
;; facts file named on the command line; each rule is a loop over the
;; relations its body joins. Each query's distribution is Roulette's, at the
;; module's level (`display-pmf`), given the evidence; the program prints
;; `roulette K true P` and `roulette K false P` for the K-th query.

(require racket/port racket/string racket/match)

;; A statement of the program: a definition, which the language does not
;; run as a query of its own (it runs each expression of the module as one).
(define-syntax-rule (statement e ...) (define-values () (begin e ... (values))))

;; the tuple t of r holds also where x does
(define (add! r t x)
  (hash-set! r t (if (hash-has-key? r t) (|| (hash-ref r t) x) x)))
;; whether the tuple t of r holds
(define (holds r t) (hash-ref r t #f))
;; whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
(define (probe r t) (if (hash-has-key? r t) (list (hash-ref r t)) null))
;; the tuples of r and whether each holds, (tuple . holding) each, by their
;; values at positions ps (from 0)
(define (index r . ps)
  (define ix (make-hash))
  (for ([(t x) (in-hash r)])
    (hash-update! ix (for/list ([p (in-list ps)]) (list-ref t p)) (λ (es) (cons (cons t x) es)) null))
  ix)
;; whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
(define (holds-any ix k)
  (for/fold ([some #f]) ([e (in-list (hash-ref ix k null))]) (|| some (cdr e))))
;; the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
;; head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
(define (choose . ps)
  (let loop ([ps ps] [left 1.0] [none #t])
    (if (null? ps)
        null
        (let* ([q (if (> left 0) (min 1.0 (/ (car ps) left)) 1.0)]
               [c (if (>= q 1.0) #t (flip q))])
          (cons (&& none c) (loop (cdr ps) (- left (car ps)) (&& none (! c))))))))

(define (constant s) (or (string->number s) (string->symbol s)))
;; the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
;; a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
(define (facts path)
  (define db (make-hash))
  (for ([line (in-lines (open-input-file path))])
    (define f (string-split line "\t" #:trim? #f))
    (define p (string->number (cadr f)))
    (add! (hash-ref! db (car f) make-hash) (map constant (cddr f)) (if (>= p 1) #t (flip p))))
  db)

;; The distribution of v, a list of (value . probability): Roulette's query
;; at the module's level (`display-pmf`), read back from the table it
;; prints, or from the one value it prints alone.
(define (distribution v)
  (define text (with-output-to-string (λ () (display-pmf v))))
  (define (datum s)
    (define d (read (open-input-string s)))
    (if (and (pair? d) (eq? (car d) 'quote)) (cadr d) d))
  (define rows
    (for/list ([line (in-list (string-split text "\n"))]
               #:when (regexp-match? #rx"[│|]" line))
      (filter (λ (s) (not (string=? s ""))) (map string-trim (regexp-split #rx"[│|]" line)))))
  (if (null? rows)
      (list (cons (datum text) 1))
      (for/list ([r (in-list rows)]
                 #:unless (equal? r '("Value" "Probability")))
        (cons (datum (car r)) (string->number (cadr r))))))
(define (real p) (if (exact? p) (exact->inexact p) p))
(define (probability dist v)
  (define e (assoc v dist))
  (if e (cdr e) 0))
(define (report dists)
  (for ([dist (in-list dists)] [k (in-naturals 1)])
    (printf "roulette ~a true ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #t)))
    (printf "roulette ~a false ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #f)))))

(define db (facts (vector-ref (current-command-line-arguments) 0)))
(define person-facts (hash-ref db "person/1" (make-hash)))
(define friend-facts (hash-ref db "friend/2" (make-hash)))

(define friend friend-facts)

(define influences (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; 0.2::influences(X,Y) :- friend(X,Y).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs friend)])
    (match-define (cons (list X Y) x1) t2)
    (add! influences (list X Y) (&& x1 (flip 0.2)))))

(define person person-facts)

(define stress (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; 0.3::stress(X) :- person(X).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs person)])
    (match-define (cons (list X) x1) t2)
    (add! stress (list X) (&& x1 (flip 0.3)))))

;; smokes/1: recursive; the rules applied in stages from no tuple, each
;; reading the stage before, until a stage adds no tuple and the stages number the tuples
(define (stage-smokes smokes)
  (define next-smokes (make-hash))
  ;; smokes(X) :- stress(X).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs stress)])
    (match-define (cons (list X) x1) t2)
    (add! next-smokes (list X) x1))
  ;; smokes(X) :- friend(X,Y), influences(Y,X), smokes(Y).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs friend)])
    (match-define (cons (list X Y) x1) t2)
    (for ([x3 (in-list (probe influences (list Y X)))])
      (for ([x4 (in-list (probe smokes (list Y)))])
        (add! next-smokes (list X) (&& x1 x3 x4)))))
  (list next-smokes))
(define-values (smokes)
  (let loop ([rels (list (make-hash))] [stage 0] [before -1])
    (define size (for/sum ([r (in-list rels)]) (hash-count r)))
    (if (or (< stage size) (not (= size before)))
        (loop (apply stage-smokes rels) (+ stage 1) size)
        (apply values rels))))

(define dists
  (list (distribution (holds smokes (list 'p1)))
        (distribution (holds smokes (list 'p2)))
        (distribution (holds smokes (list 'p3)))
        (distribution (holds smokes (list 'p4)))
        (distribution (holds smokes (list 'p5)))
        (distribution (holds smokes (list 'p6)))
        (distribution (holds smokes (list 'p7)))
        (distribution (holds smokes (list 'p8)))
        (distribution (holds smokes (list 'p9)))
        (distribution (holds smokes (list 'p10)))))
(statement (report dists))

;; nsym4.pl: a ProbLog program written for Roulette by tddlog's
;; scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a hash
;; from its tuples (lists of constants) to whether each holds, a Boolean of the
;; coins; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from the
;; facts file named on the command line; each rule is a loop over the
;; relations its body joins. Each query's distribution is Roulette's, at the
;; module's level (`display-pmf`), given the evidence; the program prints
;; `roulette K true P` and `roulette K false P` for the K-th query.

(require racket/port racket/string racket/match)

;; A statement of the program: a definition, which the language does not
;; run as a query of its own (it runs each expression of the module as one).
(define-syntax-rule (statement e ...) (define-values () (begin e ... (values))))

;; the tuple t of r holds also where x does
(define (add! r t x)
  (hash-set! r t (if (hash-has-key? r t) (|| (hash-ref r t) x) x)))
;; whether the tuple t of r holds
(define (holds r t) (hash-ref r t #f))
;; whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
(define (probe r t) (if (hash-has-key? r t) (list (hash-ref r t)) null))
;; the tuples of r and whether each holds, (tuple . holding) each, by their
;; values at positions ps (from 0)
(define (index r . ps)
  (define ix (make-hash))
  (for ([(t x) (in-hash r)])
    (hash-update! ix (for/list ([p (in-list ps)]) (list-ref t p)) (λ (es) (cons (cons t x) es)) null))
  ix)
;; whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
(define (holds-any ix k)
  (for/fold ([some #f]) ([e (in-list (hash-ref ix k null))]) (|| some (cdr e))))
;; the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
;; head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
(define (choose . ps)
  (let loop ([ps ps] [left 1.0] [none #t])
    (if (null? ps)
        null
        (let* ([q (if (> left 0) (min 1.0 (/ (car ps) left)) 1.0)]
               [c (if (>= q 1.0) #t (flip q))])
          (cons (&& none c) (loop (cdr ps) (- left (car ps)) (&& none (! c))))))))

(define (constant s) (or (string->number s) (string->symbol s)))
;; the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
;; a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
(define (facts path)
  (define db (make-hash))
  (for ([line (in-lines (open-input-file path))])
    (define f (string-split line "\t" #:trim? #f))
    (define p (string->number (cadr f)))
    (add! (hash-ref! db (car f) make-hash) (map constant (cddr f)) (if (>= p 1) #t (flip p))))

;; at the module's level (`display-pmf`), read back from the table it
;; prints, or from the one value it prints alone.
(define (distribution v)
  (define text (with-output-to-string (λ () (display-pmf v))))
  (define (datum s)
    (define d (read (open-input-string s)))
    (if (and (pair? d) (eq? (car d) 'quote)) (cadr d) d))

    (for/list ([line (in-list (string-split text "\n"))]
               #:when (regexp-match? #rx"[│|]" line))
      (filter (λ (s) (not (string=? s ""))) (map string-trim (regexp-split #rx"[│|]" line)))))

      (list (cons (datum text) 1))
      (for/list ([r (in-list rows)]
                 #:unless (equal? r '("Value" "Probability")))
        (cons (datum (car r)) (string->number (cadr r))))))

  (define e (assoc v dist))
  (if e (cdr e) 0))

    (printf "roulette ~a true ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #t)))
    (printf "roulette ~a false ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #f)))))

(define person-facts (hash-ref db "person/1" (make-hash)))
(define friend-facts (hash-ref db "friend/2" (make-hash)))

  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs friend)])
    (match-define (cons (list X Y) x1) t2)
    (add! influences (list X Y) (&& x1 (flip 0.2)))))

(define person person-facts)

(define stress (make-hash))

  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs person)])
    (match-define (cons (list X) x1) t2)

# nsym12.pl: a ProbLog program written in Julia for Alea.jl by tddlog's
# scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a
# dictionary from its tuples to whether each holds, a Dist{Bool} of the coins
# or a Bool; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from
# the facts file FACTS; each rule is a loop over the relations its body
# joins. `model()` is the queries' holdings, given the evidence (`observe`),
# in the form of tddlog's data/alea programs: Alea.jl answers them with `pr`,
# and its tddlog backend writes their circuit for tddlog.
#
#   julia --project=ALEA alea_bench.jl run --file FACTS FACTS_PATH problog.jl
using Alea

const QUERY = :pr
const FACTS = ""   # the facts file (alea_bench.jl --file FACTS PATH)

const Relation = Dict{Tuple,Any}
const NONE = Pair{Tuple,Any}[]

# the tuple t of r holds also where x does
add!(r::Relation, t::Tuple, x) = (r[t] = haskey(r, t) ? r[t] | x : x; nothing)
# whether the tuple t of r holds
holds(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = get(r, t, false)
# whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
probe(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = haskey(r, t) ? (r[t],) : ()
# the tuples of r and whether each holds, by their values at positions ps
function index(r::Relation, ps...)
    ix = Dict{Tuple,Vector{Pair{Tuple,Any}}}()
    for (t, x) in r
        push!(get!(() -> Pair{Tuple,Any}[], ix, map(p -> t[p], ps)), t => x)
    end
    ix
end
# whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
holds_any(ix, k) = reduce(|, (x for (_, x) in get(ix, k, NONE)); init = false)
# the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
# head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
function choose(ps...)
    chosen, none, left = Any[], true, 1.0
    for p in ps
        q = left > 0 ? min(p / left, 1.0) : 1.0
        c = q >= 1.0 ? true : flip(q)
        push!(chosen, none & c)
        none, left = none & !c, left - p
    end
    chosen
end

constant(s) = something(tryparse(Int, s), tryparse(Float64, s), Some(Symbol(s)))
# the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
# a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
function facts(path)
    db = Dict{String,Relation}()
    for line in eachline(path)
        f = split(line, '\t')
        p = parse(Float64, f[2])
        add!(get!(Relation, db, f[1]), Tuple(constant.(f[3:end])), p >= 1 ? true : flip(p))
    end
    db
end

function program(db)
    person_facts = get(db, "person/1", Relation())
    friend_facts = get(db, "friend/2", Relation())

    friend = friend_facts

    influences = Relation()
    # 0.2::influences(X,Y) :- friend(X,Y).
    for ((X, Y), x1) in friend
        add!(influences, (X, Y), x1 & flip(0.2))
    end

    person = person_facts

    stress = Relation()
    # 0.3::stress(X) :- person(X).
    for ((X,), x1) in person
        add!(stress, (X,), x1 & flip(0.3))
    end

    # smokes/1: recursive; the rules applied in stages from no tuple, each
    # reading the stage before, until a stage adds no tuple and the stages number the tuples
    smokes = Relation()
    stage, before = 0, -1
    while stage < length(smokes) || length(smokes) != before
        before = length(smokes)
        next_smokes = Relation()
        # smokes(X) :- stress(X).
        for ((X,), x1) in stress
            add!(next_smokes, (X,), x1)
        end
        # smokes(X) :- friend(X,Y), influences(Y,X), smokes(Y).
        for ((X, Y), x1) in friend
            for x2 in probe(influences, (Y, X))
                for x3 in probe(smokes, (Y,))
                    add!(next_smokes, (X,), x1 & x2 & x3)
                end
            end
        end
        smokes = next_smokes
        stage += 1
    end

    queries = (holds(smokes, (:p1,)), holds(smokes, (:p2,)), holds(smokes, (:p3,)), holds(smokes, (:p4,)), holds(smokes, (:p5,)), holds(smokes, (:p6,)), holds(smokes, (:p7,)), holds(smokes, (:p8,)), holds(smokes, (:p9,)), holds(smokes, (:p10,)), holds(smokes, (:p11,)), holds(smokes, (:p12,)))
    evidence = true
    queries, evidence
end

# The queries' holdings, the evidence observed: Alea's `@alea` keeps the
# observation, and the relations are built outside it, as plain Julia.
function model()
    qs, ev = program(facts(FACTS))
    ev === true && return qs
    @alea begin
        observe(ev)
        qs
    end
end

# nsym14.pl: a ProbLog program written in Julia for Alea.jl by tddlog's
# scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a
# dictionary from its tuples to whether each holds, a Dist{Bool} of the coins
# or a Bool; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from
# the facts file FACTS; each rule is a loop over the relations its body
# joins. `model()` is the queries' holdings, given the evidence (`observe`),
# in the form of tddlog's data/alea programs: Alea.jl answers them with `pr`,
# and its tddlog backend writes their circuit for tddlog.
#
#   julia --project=ALEA alea_bench.jl run --file FACTS FACTS_PATH problog.jl
using Alea

const QUERY = :pr
const FACTS = ""   # the facts file (alea_bench.jl --file FACTS PATH)

const Relation = Dict{Tuple,Any}
const NONE = Pair{Tuple,Any}[]

# the tuple t of r holds also where x does
add!(r::Relation, t::Tuple, x) = (r[t] = haskey(r, t) ? r[t] | x : x; nothing)
# whether the tuple t of r holds
holds(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = get(r, t, false)
# whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
probe(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = haskey(r, t) ? (r[t],) : ()
# the tuples of r and whether each holds, by their values at positions ps
function index(r::Relation, ps...)
    ix = Dict{Tuple,Vector{Pair{Tuple,Any}}}()
    for (t, x) in r
        push!(get!(() -> Pair{Tuple,Any}[], ix, map(p -> t[p], ps)), t => x)
    end
    ix
end
# whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
holds_any(ix, k) = reduce(|, (x for (_, x) in get(ix, k, NONE)); init = false)
# the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
# head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
function choose(ps...)
    chosen, none, left = Any[], true, 1.0
    for p in ps
        q = left > 0 ? min(p / left, 1.0) : 1.0
        c = q >= 1.0 ? true : flip(q)
        push!(chosen, none & c)
        none, left = none & !c, left - p
    end
    chosen
end

constant(s) = something(tryparse(Int, s), tryparse(Float64, s), Some(Symbol(s)))
# the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
# a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
function facts(path)
    db = Dict{String,Relation}()
    for line in eachline(path)
        f = split(line, '\t')
        p = parse(Float64, f[2])
        add!(get!(Relation, db, f[1]), Tuple(constant.(f[3:end])), p >= 1 ? true : flip(p))
    end
    db
end

function program(db)
    person_facts = get(db, "person/1", Relation())
    friend_facts = get(db, "friend/2", Relation())

    friend = friend_facts

    influences = Relation()
    # 0.2::influences(X,Y) :- friend(X,Y).
    for ((X, Y), x1) in friend
        add!(influences, (X, Y), x1 & flip(0.2))
    end

    person = person_facts

    stress = Relation()
    # 0.3::stress(X) :- person(X).
    for ((X,), x1) in person
        add!(stress, (X,), x1 & flip(0.3))
    end

    # smokes/1: recursive; the rules applied in stages from no tuple, each
    # reading the stage before, until a stage adds no tuple and the stages number the tuples
    smokes = Relation()
    stage, before = 0, -1
    while stage < length(smokes) || length(smokes) != before
        before = length(smokes)
        next_smokes = Relation()
        # smokes(X) :- stress(X).
        for ((X,), x1) in stress
            add!(next_smokes, (X,), x1)
        end
        # smokes(X) :- friend(X,Y), influences(Y,X), smokes(Y).
        for ((X, Y), x1) in friend
            for x2 in probe(influences, (Y, X))
                for x3 in probe(smokes, (Y,))
                    add!(next_smokes, (X,), x1 & x2 & x3)
                end
            end
        end
        smokes = next_smokes
        stage += 1
    end

    queries = (holds(smokes, (:p1,)), holds(smokes, (:p2,)), holds(smokes, (:p3,)), holds(smokes, (:p4,)), holds(smokes, (:p5,)), holds(smokes, (:p6,)), holds(smokes, (:p7,)), holds(smokes, (:p8,)), holds(smokes, (:p9,)), holds(smokes, (:p10,)), holds(smokes, (:p11,)), holds(smokes, (:p12,)), holds(smokes, (:p13,)), holds(smokes, (:p14,)))
    evidence = true
    queries, evidence
end

# The queries' holdings, the evidence observed: Alea's `@alea` keeps the
# observation, and the relations are built outside it, as plain Julia.
function model()
    qs, ev = program(facts(FACTS))
    ev === true && return qs
    @alea begin
        observe(ev)
        qs
    end
end

;; nsym6.pl: a ProbLog program written in Pluck by tddlog's scripts/problog2ppl.py,
;; first order as it is written. A relation is a list of its tuples, each (Pair
;; TUPLE HOLDING), a symbol a constructor of its own and an integer a natural;
;; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), drawn once; each rule a
;; concat_map over the relations its body joins, a tuple that several instances
;; give holding where one does (`union`). Query cK asks the K-th query, given the
;; evidence.

(define-type weight (Sure) (Chance p))
(define (draw w) (match w Sure => (True) Chance p => (flip p)))
(define (draw_all fs) (map (lambda f -> (Pair (fst f) (draw (snd f)))) fs))
;; rel with the tuple t, holding where v does too
(define (insert eq t v rel)
  (match rel
    Nil => (Cons (Pair t v) (Nil))
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) t) (Cons (Pair t (or (snd e) v)) rest) (Cons e (insert eq t v rest)))))
(define (union eq rel xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => rel
    Cons x rest => (union eq (insert eq (fst x) (snd x) rel) rest)))
;; whether the tuple t of rel holds; whether one of the tuples that p accepts does
(define (holds eq rel t)
  (match rel
    Nil => (False)
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) t) (snd e) (holds eq rest t))))
(define (any_holds p rel)
  (match rel
    Nil => (False)
    Cons e rest => (if (p (fst e)) (or (snd e) (any_holds p rest)) (any_holds p rest))))
(define (concat_map f xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => (Nil)
    Cons x rest => (append (f x) (concat_map f rest))))
(define (between lo hi) (if (> lo hi) (Nil) (Cons lo (between (S lo) hi))))
(define (size_of rels) (fold (lambda acc r -> (+ acc (length r))) 0 rels))
;; the coins of a probabilistic rule in a recursion, kept by instance across the stages: the
;; instances xs, each (Pair KEY (Pair BODY HEADS)), with the coin of each KEY in table (a new
;; one drawn where it has none): (Pair TABLE' the heads, each (Pair TUPLE HOLDING))
(define (coin_of eq k table)
  (match table
    Nil => (Pair (False) (False))
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) k) (Pair (True) (snd e)) (coin_of eq k rest))))
(define (attach eq draw pick table xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => (Pair table (Nil))
    Cons x rest =>
    (let ((found (coin_of eq (fst x) table))
          (c (if (fst found) (snd found) (draw)))
          (table2 (if (fst found) table (Cons (Pair (fst x) c) table)))
          (more (attach eq draw pick table2 rest))
          (body (fst (snd x))))
      (Pair (fst more) (append (mapi (lambda h i -> (Pair h (and body (pick c i)))) (snd (snd x))) (snd more))))))

(define-type sym (c_p1) (c_p2) (c_p3) (c_p4) (c_p5) (c_p6))
(define-type tuple1 (T1 a1))
(define-type tuple2 (T2 a1 a2))
(define (eq_person a b) (match a T1 a1 => (match b T1 b1 => (constructor=? a1 b1))))
(define (eq_friend a b) (match a T2 a1 a2 => (match b T2 b1 b2 => (and (constructor=? a1 b1) (constructor=? a2 b2)))))
(define (eq_stress a b) (match a T1 a1 => (match b T1 b1 => (constructor=? a1 b1))))
(define (eq_influences a b) (match a T2 a1 a2 => (match b T2 b1 b2 => (and (constructor=? a1 b1) (constructor=? a2 b2)))))
(define (eq_smokes a b) (match a T1 a1 => (match b T1 b1 => (constructor=? a1 b1))))

;; person/1: 6 facts
(define person_facts
  (Cons (Pair (T1 (c_p1)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T1 (c_p2)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T1 (c_p3)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T1 (c_p4)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T1 (c_p5)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T1 (c_p6)) (Sure))
  (Nil))))))))
;; friend/2: 24 facts
(define friend_facts
  (Cons (Pair (T2 (c_p2) (c_p1)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T2 (c_p1) (c_p2)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T2 (c_p3) (c_p2)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T2 (c_p2) (c_p3)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T2 (c_p3) (c_p1)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T2 (c_p1) (c_p3)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T2 (c_p4) (c_p3)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T2 (c_p3) (c_p4)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T2 (c_p4) (c_p2)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T2 (c_p2) (c_p4)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T2 (c_p4) (c_p1)) (Sure))

#lang roulette/example/disrupt
;; nsym14.pl: a ProbLog program written for Roulette by tddlog's
;; scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a hash
;; from its tuples (lists of constants) to whether each holds, a Boolean of the
;; coins; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from the
;; facts file named on the command line; each rule is a loop over the
;; relations its body joins. Each query's distribution is Roulette's, at the
;; module's level (`display-pmf`), given the evidence; the program prints
;; `roulette K true P` and `roulette K false P` for the K-th query.

(require racket/port racket/string racket/match)

;; A statement of the program: a definition, which the language does not
;; run as a query of its own (it runs each expression of the module as one).
(define-syntax-rule (statement e ...) (define-values () (begin e ... (values))))

;; the tuple t of r holds also where x does
(define (add! r t x)
  (hash-set! r t (if (hash-has-key? r t) (|| (hash-ref r t) x) x)))
;; whether the tuple t of r holds
(define (holds r t) (hash-ref r t #f))
;; whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
(define (probe r t) (if (hash-has-key? r t) (list (hash-ref r t)) null))
;; the tuples of r and whether each holds, (tuple . holding) each, by their
;; values at positions ps (from 0)
(define (index r . ps)
  (define ix (make-hash))
  (for ([(t x) (in-hash r)])
    (hash-update! ix (for/list ([p (in-list ps)]) (list-ref t p)) (λ (es) (cons (cons t x) es)) null))
  ix)
;; whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
(define (holds-any ix k)
  (for/fold ([some #f]) ([e (in-list (hash-ref ix k null))]) (|| some (cdr e))))
;; the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
;; head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
(define (choose . ps)
  (let loop ([ps ps] [left 1.0] [none #t])
    (if (null? ps)
        null
        (let* ([q (if (> left 0) (min 1.0 (/ (car ps) left)) 1.0)]
               [c (if (>= q 1.0) #t (flip q))])
          (cons (&& none c) (loop (cdr ps) (- left (car ps)) (&& none (! c))))))))

(define (constant s) (or (string->number s) (string->symbol s)))
;; the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
;; a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
(define (facts path)
  (define db (make-hash))
  (for ([line (in-lines (open-input-file path))])
    (define f (string-split line "\t" #:trim? #f))
    (define p (string->number (cadr f)))
    (add! (hash-ref! db (car f) make-hash) (map constant (cddr f)) (if (>= p 1) #t (flip p))))
  db)

;; The distribution of v, a list of (value . probability): Roulette's query
;; at the module's level (`display-pmf`), read back from the table it
;; prints, or from the one value it prints alone.
(define (distribution v)
  (define text (with-output-to-string (λ () (display-pmf v))))
  (define (datum s)
    (define d (read (open-input-string s)))
    (if (and (pair? d) (eq? (car d) 'quote)) (cadr d) d))
  (define rows
    (for/list ([line (in-list (string-split text "\n"))]
               #:when (regexp-match? #rx"[│|]" line))
      (filter (λ (s) (not (string=? s ""))) (map string-trim (regexp-split #rx"[│|]" line)))))
  (if (null? rows)
      (list (cons (datum text) 1))
      (for/list ([r (in-list rows)]
                 #:unless (equal? r '("Value" "Probability")))
        (cons (datum (car r)) (string->number (cadr r))))))
(define (real p) (if (exact? p) (exact->inexact p) p))
(define (probability dist v)
  (define e (assoc v dist))
  (if e (cdr e) 0))
(define (report dists)
  (for ([dist (in-list dists)] [k (in-naturals 1)])
    (printf "roulette ~a true ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #t)))
    (printf "roulette ~a false ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #f)))))

(define db (facts (vector-ref (current-command-line-arguments) 0)))
(define person-facts (hash-ref db "person/1" (make-hash)))
(define friend-facts (hash-ref db "friend/2" (make-hash)))

(define friend friend-facts)

(define influences (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; 0.2::influences(X,Y) :- friend(X,Y).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs friend)])
    (match-define (cons (list X Y) x1) t2)
    (add! influences (list X Y) (&& x1 (flip 0.2)))))

(define person person-facts)

(define stress (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; 0.3::stress(X) :- person(X).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs person)])
    (match-define (cons (list X) x1) t2)
    (add! stress (list X) (&& x1 (flip 0.3)))))

;; smokes/1: recursive; the rules applied in stages from no tuple, each
;; reading the stage before, until a stage adds no tuple and the stages number the tuples
(define (stage-smokes smokes)
  (define next-smokes (make-hash))
  ;; smokes(X) :- stress(X).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs stress)])
    (match-define (cons (list X) x1) t2)
    (add! next-smokes (list X) x1))
  ;; smokes(X) :- friend(X,Y), influences(Y,X), smokes(Y).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs friend)])
    (match-define (cons (list X Y) x1) t2)
    (for ([x3 (in-list (probe influences (list Y X)))])
      (for ([x4 (in-list (probe smokes (list Y)))])
        (add! next-smokes (list X) (&& x1 x3 x4)))))
  (list next-smokes))
(define-values (smokes)
  (let loop ([rels (list (make-hash))] [stage 0] [before -1])
    (define size (for/sum ([r (in-list rels)]) (hash-count r)))
    (if (or (< stage size) (not (= size before)))
        (loop (apply stage-smokes rels) (+ stage 1) size)
        (apply values rels))))

(define dists
  (list (distribution (holds smokes (list 'p1)))
        (distribution (holds smokes (list 'p2)))
        (distribution (holds smokes (list 'p3)))
        (distribution (holds smokes (list 'p4)))
        (distribution (holds smokes (list 'p5)))
        (distribution (holds smokes (list 'p6)))
        (distribution (holds smokes (list 'p7)))
        (distribution (holds smokes (list 'p8)))
        (distribution (holds smokes (list 'p9)))
        (distribution (holds smokes (list 'p10)))
        (distribution (holds smokes (list 'p11)))
        (distribution (holds smokes (list 'p12)))
        (distribution (holds smokes (list 'p13)))
        (distribution (holds smokes (list 'p14)))))
(statement (report dists))

#lang roulette/example/disrupt
;; nsym8.pl: a ProbLog program written for Roulette by tddlog's
;; scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a hash
;; from its tuples (lists of constants) to whether each holds, a Boolean of the
;; coins; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from the
;; facts file named on the command line; each rule is a loop over the
;; relations its body joins. Each query's distribution is Roulette's, at the
;; module's level (`display-pmf`), given the evidence; the program prints
;; `roulette K true P` and `roulette K false P` for the K-th query.

(require racket/port racket/string racket/match)

;; A statement of the program: a definition, which the language does not
;; run as a query of its own (it runs each expression of the module as one).
(define-syntax-rule (statement e ...) (define-values () (begin e ... (values))))

;; the tuple t of r holds also where x does
(define (add! r t x)
  (hash-set! r t (if (hash-has-key? r t) (|| (hash-ref r t) x) x)))
;; whether the tuple t of r holds
(define (holds r t) (hash-ref r t #f))
;; whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
(define (probe r t) (if (hash-has-key? r t) (list (hash-ref r t)) null))
;; the tuples of r and whether each holds, (tuple . holding) each, by their
;; values at positions ps (from 0)
(define (index r . ps)
  (define ix (make-hash))
  (for ([(t x) (in-hash r)])
    (hash-update! ix (for/list ([p (in-list ps)]) (list-ref t p)) (λ (es) (cons (cons t x) es)) null))
  ix)
;; whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
(define (holds-any ix k)
  (for/fold ([some #f]) ([e (in-list (hash-ref ix k null))]) (|| some (cdr e))))
;; the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
;; head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
(define (choose . ps)
  (let loop ([ps ps] [left 1.0] [none #t])
    (if (null? ps)
        null
        (let* ([q (if (> left 0) (min 1.0 (/ (car ps) left)) 1.0)]
               [c (if (>= q 1.0) #t (flip q))])
          (cons (&& none c) (loop (cdr ps) (- left (car ps)) (&& none (! c))))))))

(define (constant s) (or (string->number s) (string->symbol s)))
;; the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
;; a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
(define (facts path)
  (define db (make-hash))
  (for ([line (in-lines (open-input-file path))])
    (define f (string-split line "\t" #:trim? #f))
    (define p (string->number (cadr f)))
    (add! (hash-ref! db (car f) make-hash) (map constant (cddr f)) (if (>= p 1) #t (flip p))))
  db)

;; The distribution of v, a list of (value . probability): Roulette's query
;; at the module's level (`display-pmf`), read back from the table it
;; prints, or from the one value it prints alone.
(define (distribution v)
  (define text (with-output-to-string (λ () (display-pmf v))))
  (define (datum s)
    (define d (read (open-input-string s)))
    (if (and (pair? d) (eq? (car d) 'quote)) (cadr d) d))
  (define rows
    (for/list ([line (in-list (string-split text "\n"))]
               #:when (regexp-match? #rx"[│|]" line))
      (filter (λ (s) (not (string=? s ""))) (map string-trim (regexp-split #rx"[│|]" line)))))
  (if (null? rows)
      (list (cons (datum text) 1))
      (for/list ([r (in-list rows)]
                 #:unless (equal? r '("Value" "Probability")))
        (cons (datum (car r)) (string->number (cadr r))))))
(define (real p) (if (exact? p) (exact->inexact p) p))
(define (probability dist v)
  (define e (assoc v dist))
  (if e (cdr e) 0))
(define (report dists)
  (for ([dist (in-list dists)] [k (in-naturals 1)])
    (printf "roulette ~a true ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #t)))
    (printf "roulette ~a false ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #f)))))

(define db (facts (vector-ref (current-command-line-arguments) 0)))
(define person-facts (hash-ref db "person/1" (make-hash)))
(define friend-facts (hash-ref db "friend/2" (make-hash)))

(define friend friend-facts)

(define influences (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; 0.2::influences(X,Y) :- friend(X,Y).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs friend)])
    (match-define (cons (list X Y) x1) t2)
    (add! influences (list X Y) (&& x1 (flip 0.2)))))

(define person person-facts)

(define stress (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; 0.3::stress(X) :- person(X).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs person)])
    (match-define (cons (list X) x1) t2)
    (add! stress (list X) (&& x1 (flip 0.3)))))

;; smokes/1: recursive; the rules applied in stages from no tuple, each
;; reading the stage before, until a stage adds no tuple and the stages number the tuples
(define (stage-smokes smokes)
  (define next-smokes (make-hash))
  ;; smokes(X) :- stress(X).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs stress)])
    (match-define (cons (list X) x1) t2)
    (add! next-smokes (list X) x1))
  ;; smokes(X) :- friend(X,Y), influences(Y,X), smokes(Y).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs friend)])
    (match-define (cons (list X Y) x1) t2)
    (for ([x3 (in-list (probe influences (list Y X)))])
      (for ([x4 (in-list (probe smokes (list Y)))])
        (add! next-smokes (list X) (&& x1 x3 x4)))))
  (list next-smokes))
(define-values (smokes)
  (let loop ([rels (list (make-hash))] [stage 0] [before -1])
    (define size (for/sum ([r (in-list rels)]) (hash-count r)))
    (if (or (< stage size) (not (= size before)))
        (loop (apply stage-smokes rels) (+ stage 1) size)
        (apply values rels))))

(define dists
  (list (distribution (holds smokes (list 'p1)))
        (distribution (holds smokes (list 'p2)))
        (distribution (holds smokes (list 'p3)))
        (distribution (holds smokes (list 'p4)))
        (distribution (holds smokes (list 'p5)))
        (distribution (holds smokes (list 'p6)))
        (distribution (holds smokes (list 'p7)))
        (distribution (holds smokes (list 'p8)))))
(statement (report dists))

;; nsym14.pl: a ProbLog program written in Pluck by tddlog's scripts/problog2ppl.py,
;; first order as it is written. A relation is a list of its tuples, each (Pair
;; TUPLE HOLDING), a symbol a constructor of its own and an integer a natural;
;; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), drawn once; each rule a
;; concat_map over the relations its body joins, a tuple that several instances
;; give holding where one does (`union`). Query cK asks the K-th query, given the
;; evidence.

(define-type weight (Sure) (Chance p))
(define (draw w) (match w Sure => (True) Chance p => (flip p)))
(define (draw_all fs) (map (lambda f -> (Pair (fst f) (draw (snd f)))) fs))
;; rel with the tuple t, holding where v does too
(define (insert eq t v rel)
  (match rel
    Nil => (Cons (Pair t v) (Nil))
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) t) (Cons (Pair t (or (snd e) v)) rest) (Cons e (insert eq t v rest)))))
(define (union eq rel xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => rel
    Cons x rest => (union eq (insert eq (fst x) (snd x) rel) rest)))
;; whether the tuple t of rel holds; whether one of the tuples that p accepts does
(define (holds eq rel t)
  (match rel
    Nil => (False)
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) t) (snd e) (holds eq rest t))))
(define (any_holds p rel)
  (match rel
    Nil => (False)
    Cons e rest => (if (p (fst e)) (or (snd e) (any_holds p rest)) (any_holds p rest))))
(define (concat_map f xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => (Nil)
    Cons x rest => (append (f x) (concat_map f rest))))
(define (between lo hi) (if (> lo hi) (Nil) (Cons lo (between (S lo) hi))))
(define (size_of rels) (fold (lambda acc r -> (+ acc (length r))) 0 rels))
;; the coins of a probabilistic rule in a recursion, kept by instance across the stages: the
;; instances xs, each (Pair KEY (Pair BODY HEADS)), with the coin of each KEY in table (a new
;; one drawn where it has none): (Pair TABLE' the heads, each (Pair TUPLE HOLDING))
(define (coin_of eq k table)
  (match table
    Nil => (Pair (False) (False))
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) k) (Pair (True) (snd e)) (coin_of eq k rest))))
(define (attach eq draw pick table xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => (Pair table (Nil))
    Cons x rest =>
    (let ((found (coin_of eq (fst x) table))
          (c (if (fst found) (snd found) (draw)))
          (table2 (if (fst found) table (Cons (Pair (fst x) c) table)))

# nsym16.pl: a ProbLog program written in Julia for Alea.jl by tddlog's
# scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a
# dictionary from its tuples to whether each holds, a Dist{Bool} of the coins
# or a Bool; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from
# the facts file FACTS; each rule is a loop over the relations its body
# joins. `model()` is the queries' holdings, given the evidence (`observe`),
# in the form of tddlog's data/alea programs: Alea.jl answers them with `pr`,
# and its tddlog backend writes their circuit for tddlog.
#
#   julia --project=ALEA alea_bench.jl run --file FACTS FACTS_PATH problog.jl
using Alea

const QUERY = :pr
const FACTS = ""   # the facts file (alea_bench.jl --file FACTS PATH)

const Relation = Dict{Tuple,Any}
const NONE = Pair{Tuple,Any}[]

# the tuple t of r holds also where x does
add!(r::Relation, t::Tuple, x) = (r[t] = haskey(r, t) ? r[t] | x : x; nothing)
# whether the tuple t of r holds
holds(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = get(r, t, false)
# whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
probe(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = haskey(r, t) ? (r[t],) : ()
# the tuples of r and whether each holds, by their values at positions ps
function index(r::Relation, ps...)
    ix = Dict{Tuple,Vector{Pair{Tuple,Any}}}()
    for (t, x) in r
        push!(get!(() -> Pair{Tuple,Any}[], ix, map(p -> t[p], ps)), t => x)
    end
    ix
end
# whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
holds_any(ix, k) = reduce(|, (x for (_, x) in get(ix, k, NONE)); init = false)
# the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
# head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
function choose(ps...)
    chosen, none, left = Any[], true, 1.0
    for p in ps
        q = left > 0 ? min(p / left, 1.0) : 1.0
        c = q >= 1.0 ? true : flip(q)
        push!(chosen, none & c)
        none, left = none & !c, left - p
    end
    chosen
end

constant(s) = something(tryparse(Int, s), tryparse(Float64, s), Some(Symbol(s)))
# the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
# a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
function facts(path)
    db = Dict{String,Relation}()
    for line in eachline(path)
        f = split(line, '\t')
        p = parse(Float64, f[2])
        add!(get!(Relation, db, f[1]), Tuple(constant.(f[3:end])), p >= 1 ? true : flip(p))
    end
    db
end

function program(db)
    person_facts = get(db, "person/1", Relation())
    friend_facts = get(db, "friend/2", Relation())

    friend = friend_facts

    influences = Relation()
    # 0.2::influences(X,Y) :- friend(X,Y).
    for ((X, Y), x1) in friend
        add!(influences, (X, Y), x1 & flip(0.2))
    end

    person = person_facts

    stress = Relation()
    # 0.3::stress(X) :- person(X).
    for ((X,), x1) in person
        add!(stress, (X,), x1 & flip(0.3))
    end

    # smokes/1: recursive; the rules applied in stages from no tuple, each
    # reading the stage before, until a stage adds no tuple and the stages number the tuples
    smokes = Relation()
    stage, before = 0, -1
    while stage < length(smokes) || length(smokes) != before
        before = length(smokes)
        next_smokes = Relation()
        # smokes(X) :- stress(X).
        for ((X,), x1) in stress
            add!(next_smokes, (X,), x1)
        end
        # smokes(X) :- friend(X,Y), influences(Y,X), smokes(Y).
        for ((X, Y), x1) in friend
            for x2 in probe(influences, (Y, X))
                for x3 in probe(smokes, (Y,))
                    add!(next_smokes, (X,), x1 & x2 & x3)
                end
            end
        end
        smokes = next_smokes
        stage += 1
    end

    queries = (holds(smokes, (:p1,)), holds(smokes, (:p2,)), holds(smokes, (:p3,)), holds(smokes, (:p4,)), holds(smokes, (:p5,)), holds(smokes, (:p6,)), holds(smokes, (:p7,)), holds(smokes, (:p8,)), holds(smokes, (:p9,)), holds(smokes, (:p10,)), holds(smokes, (:p11,)), holds(smokes, (:p12,)), holds(smokes, (:p13,)), holds(smokes, (:p14,)), holds(smokes, (:p15,)), holds(smokes, (:p16,)))
    evidence = true
    queries, evidence
end

# The queries' holdings, the evidence observed: Alea's `@alea` keeps the
# observation, and the relations are built outside it, as plain Julia.
function model()
    qs, ev = program(facts(FACTS))
    ev === true && return qs
    @alea begin
        observe(ev)
        qs
    end
end
